free_tier.stated: No free tier: plans start at $20 a month, charged when you subscribe and renewing monthly until you cancel; the first month buys 100 running sandboxes and machine time at $0.036 an hour for the default 4 vCPU, 8 GB, 50 GB size, billed by the second.
free_tier.notes: The $20 plan returns the whole $20 as machine time; it is about 555 hours of the default size. A wallet without a plan has 10 GB of stopped storage, and no sandboxes can be created without a plan and card.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a machine, not a stored object; a command output keeps 8 MiB per stream and a file upload is limited by the 413 file_too_large error without a published size

retention.stated: A stopped sandbox keeps its disk and memory snapshot free for 14 days after it last stopped; named snapshots are kept until deleted, and all stopped data counts toward the plan's included storage (50 GB on the $20 plan).

egress.terms: not metered: 'Do you bill bandwidth? No.' Outbound traffic is not priced, and each sandbox gets a public IPv6 address and HTTPS URLs for its ports.

interface_detail: A documented REST API with an OpenAPI spec, a static sbx CLI, TypeScript, Python and Daytona-compatible SDKs, plus SSH and SCP into each full Ubuntu 24.04 microVM.
tooling: curl -fsSL https://sandboxer.com/install | sh installs the sbx CLI; sbx new, sbx exec, sbx ssh, sbx host and sbx fork, and the Python and TypeScript SDKs mirror the API.
chaining: A stopped sandbox resumes from a memory snapshot with its processes intact, which makes a warmed dev server reusable across agent tasks; with no charge for bandwidth, it can serve traffic directly on a public HTTPS port without a separate egress service.

limits.value: $20 a month of machine time at $0.036 an hour for the default size; time packs of $20 never expire
600 API calls a minute per API key, with short bursts up to 300 requests and a refill of 10 a second
stopped sandboxes and automatic snapshots are kept 14 days after the last stop; named snapshots until deleted
creating, forking or restoring a sandbox answers 402 payment_method_required until a card and plan are added; xlarge requires the $100 plan

limits_note: The $20 plan runs 100 sandboxes at once with 12 starts a minute, 60 an hour and 200 a day. Above each window, starts cost $0.03 to $0.07 each up to 3x the limit, then are refused. Storage is 50 GB on the $20 plan and is not billed, but it blocks new sandboxes when full.
binding_note: With no free tier and no way to start a sandbox without a plan and a card, the payment gate stops use before the monthly $20 of machine time or the 600-per-minute API rate does.

identity_cost.detail: Sign in uses GitHub, Google, an email code, or an email and password. A card is required to start any sandbox: 'Choosing one (dashboard Billing, or sbx billing plan 20) adds your card and charges the first month right away. There's no free trial.' Without a card the dashboard, docs and CLI are usable, but every create answers 402 payment_method_required. No phone or identity document is asked for.

reliability_note: At zero balance, creates and resumes fail with 402, running sandboxes get a 24-hour grace period and are then stopped with memory and disk kept. Over included storage, new sandboxes wait until data is deleted or the plan is upgraded; auto-delete, off by default, removes least-recently-used stopped sandboxes with at least 7 days' notice. A trial that started before the free trial ended slows a sandbox using 90% of its vCPUs to 1 vCPU.
confidence_note: The prices, plans, free-tier answer, storage, bandwidth answer, sign-in methods, card requirement and limits are read from the vendor's pricing, billing, quickstart and limits pages on 2026-11-25 and quoted below.
